title: Tensor exterior quotient kernel over an ordinary ring
statement: Let R be any commutative ring and A,K,B,C R-modules. Use exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Suppose f:K→B and g:B→C are linear, range(f)=ker(g), and g is surjective. For every r,s≥0, the kernel of id tensor exteriorPower.map s g on exteriorPower r A tensor exteriorPower s B is contained in the R-span of wedge(a) tensor wedge(c) where a is an r-tuple, c is an s-tuple, and c_j=f(d) for some j in Fin s and d in K. No injectivity or flatness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: quotient lift independence; stalk algebra portion of lem-sc-exterior-tensor-kernel-locally-spanned

proof.text: Let J be the span of wedges with one entry f(d). Compose the universal alternating wedge with J.mkQ. Replacing a single argument by another with the same g-image changes its value by a wedge with an entry in range(f), hence zero. Induct on a finite set of coordinates to show invariance under replacing all arguments with equal g-images. Choose a set-theoretic right inverse of the proved surjective map g and compose it coordinatewise with this alternating map. Lift independence proves its additivity, scalar compatibility and alternating property. Apply exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv to obtain L. On wedges L composed with exteriorPower.map s g equals J.mkQ; linearMap_ext proves this on the whole exterior power. Hence an element in that exterior kernel maps to zero under J.mkQ and belongs to J.

The exterior map is surjective by Mathlib exteriorPower.map_surjective. Mathlib lTensor_exact applied to its kernel inclusion identifies the tensor kernel with the range of the tensor of that inclusion. Express a preimage as a sum of pure tensors using TensorProduct.induction_on. Expand the first factor using exteriorPower.ιMulti_span and Submodule.span_induction, then expand the kernel entry using the previous step. Every resulting pure tensor is one of the claimed generators. Additions and scalar multiples are preserved by the submodule. The proof also applies in degree zero.

lean.statement:
theorem tensor_quotient_kernel_le_span
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {A : Type v₁} {K : Type v₂} {B : Type v₃} {C : Type v₄}
    [AddCommGroup A] [AddCommGroup K] [AddCommGroup B] [AddCommGroup C]
    [Module R A] [Module R K] [Module R B] [Module R C]
    (f : K →ₗ[R] B) (g : B →ₗ[R] C)
    (hfg : LinearMap.range f = LinearMap.ker g) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (r s : ℕ) :
    LinearMap.ker (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : (⋀[R]^r A) →ₗ[R] ⋀[R]^r A)
      (exteriorPower.map s g)) ≤
      Submodule.span R {z | ∃ (a : Fin r → A) (c : Fin s → B) (j : Fin s) (d : K),
        c j = f d ∧ z = exteriorPower.ιMulti R r a ⊗ₜ[R] exteriorPower.ιMulti R s c}
